content.text: No HTTP error codes anywhere, and log volume is nearly flat. I'll compare latency by span name across the two periods to find which operations shifted.

input.query: WITH a AS (SELECT service_name, span_name, attr_span_kind k, count(*) n, quantile_cont(duration,0.5)/1e6 p50, quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6 p95 FROM abnormal_traces GROUP BY 1,2,3), n AS (SELECT service_name, span_name, attr_span_kind k, count(*) n, quantile_cont(duration,0.5)/1e6 p50, quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6 p95 FROM normal_traces GROUP BY 1,2,3) SELECT a.service_name, a.span_name, a.k, n.n n_norm, a.n n_abn, round(n.p50,3) p50_n, round(a.p50,3) p50_a, round(n.p95,3) p95_n, round(a.p95,3) p95_a FROM a JOIN n USING (service_name, span_name, k) ORDER BY (a.p95/NULLIF(n.p95,0)) DESC LIMIT 40

content.text: Latency is almost entirely flat; the only real shift is `HTTP /user` p95 (0.6→1.07 ms, small sample). I'll compare metric averages per service and metric to find the real signal.

input.query: WITH a AS (SELECT service_name svc, metric, avg(value) av, stddev(value) sa FROM abnormal_metrics GROUP BY 1,2), n AS (SELECT service_name svc, metric, avg(value) nv, stddev(value) sn FROM normal_metrics GROUP BY 1,2) SELECT a.svc, a.metric, round(n.nv,3) norm_avg, round(a.av,3) abn_avg, round((a.av-n.nv)/NULLIF(n.sn,0),2) z FROM a JOIN n USING (svc, metric) WHERE abs((a.av-n.nv)/NULLIF(n.sn,0)) > 2 OR (n.nv=0 AND a.av<>0) ORDER BY abs(z) DESC

content.text: Geo stands out: container CPU jumped from ~0.003 to ~1.56 and memory rose ~50%, while its span latency stayed flat. I'll look at geo's CPU and memory time series in the abnormal window.

content.text: These logs are benign (expected authentication warnings present in both periods). Next I'll check reservation's child spans, since `MakeReservation` server p95 rose from 2.7 to 4.0 ms while its memcached child stayed flat.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' src, service_name, span_name, attr_span_kind k, count(*) n, round(avg(duration)/1e6,3) avg_ms, round(quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6,3) p95 FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name IN ('reservation','user','profile','search','rate') GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', service_name, span_name, attr_span_kind, count(*), round(avg(duration)/1e6,3), round(quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6,3) FROM normal_traces WHERE service_name IN ('reservation','user','profile','search','rate') GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 ORDER BY 2,3,1

content.text: Span-level stats are nearly identical across periods, so any fault may be localized in time and hidden by whole-window averages. I'll bucket key spans by minute across the abnormal window.

input.query: SELECT floor((epoch(time) - (SELECT min(epoch(time)) FROM abnormal_traces))/60) min_bucket, service_name, count(*) n, round(quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6,2) p95_ms, round(avg(duration)/1e6,2) avg_ms FROM abnormal_traces WHERE attr_span_kind='Server' GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 2,1

content.text: Per-minute data is flat too: no onset, and frontend/search/geo p95 hold steady. Before concluding, I'll check tail latencies (max and p99) for the geo and frontend-to-geo calls, since a few slow calls would not move p95.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' src, service_name, span_name, count(*) n, round(quantile_cont(duration,0.99)/1e6,3) p99, round(max(duration)/1e6,3) mx FROM abnormal_traces WHERE span_name IN ('geo.Geo/Nearby','search.Search/Nearby','HTTP /user','HTTP /reservation','reservation.Reservation/MakeReservation','HTTP /hotels') GROUP BY 1,2,3 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', service_name, span_name, count(*), round(quantile_cont(duration,0.99)/1e6,3), round(max(duration)/1e6,3) FROM normal_traces WHERE span_name IN ('geo.Geo/Nearby','search.Search/Nearby','HTTP /user','HTTP /reservation','reservation.Reservation/MakeReservation','HTTP /hotels') GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 3,1

content.text: I'm stopping here. The telemetry supports one clear fault, but its effect on user-facing latency is not measurable.

input.reflection: Findings: no span errors, no HTTP >=300 codes, no restarts, no new pods, log volume flat. Span latencies flat per service and per minute; per-minute trends show no onset. The one large, sustained change is geo: container/pod CPU usage ~0.003 -> ~1.56 cores from the start of the window (plateau 1.0-1.6), and working set +50% (18MB -> 27MB). Geo's own spans are unchanged (p95 0.19->0.20ms), and search->geo client spans are unchanged. Other shifts (HTTP /user, HTTP /reservation, mongodb page faults) are small-sample or tiny. Conclusion: geo container CPU saturation is the only real fault; its propagation to users is not visible in latency, so I report it with that caveat and link search->frontend as the call path to the user tier.
